title: Comparison of Periodized and Non-Periodized Resistance Training on Maximal Strength: A Meta-Analysis
population: 18 studies published from 1988 to 2015 (81 effects), comparing periodized and non-periodized groups.
key_findings: Periodized training improved 1RM more than non-periodized training, a moderate effect (effect size 0.43).
Undulating programmes were more favourable, untrained participants improved more, and higher frequency and longer studies were associated with larger 1RM gains.
The authors conclude that variation in the training stimulus appears important for maximal strength.
methods: Meta-analysis with random-effects models and moderator analysis of 1RM squat, bench press or leg press outcomes; English-language peer-reviewed studies only.
limitations: Strength outcomes only; English-language studies only; the abstract does not state whether volume was equated between groups.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
